text: A well-designed API is easy to use and understand. REST APIs organise data around resources, and each resource should have clear, predictable endpoints, such as /users or /orders. Always return the correct HTTP status codes so clients know what happened: 200 for success, 404 when something is missing, and 500 for server errors. Good documentation explains every endpoint, the parameters it accepts, and the responses it returns. Finally, use versioning, like /v1/users, so you can improve your API without breaking existing applications. Follow these practices, and developers will enjoy working with your API.
